name: Advanced Feature Engineering Patterns
description: This module describes advanced patterns for feature engineering intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.
content:
This module describes advanced patterns for feature engineering intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple feature engineering strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Measure before optimizing any feature engineering bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. State assumptions about feature engineering explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Document any non-obvious feature engineering decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Keep feature engineering changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Prefer explicit, readable feature engineering solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
7. When feature engineering decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Validate feature engineering outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. When feature engineering guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
10. Surface known limitations of a chosen feature engineering approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of feature engineering correctness.
- Do not silently drop feature engineering edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated feature engineering concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not apply generic feature engineering advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for feature engineering, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
